justification: Adds a visible prompt above the assessment tabs that opens the existing feedback widget, and changes what the widget sends: the tab it was opened from and, for four new roles, the role are written into the message text, and the new roles go to the API as 'other'. Nine files across a page, a shared widget, a helper and tests, so the three-file floor for the minor tier is exceeded. The submit payload reaches a production table through an existing route, which is why this is not treated as a copy change.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: The widget sends a role the user_type column might reject, drops the tab from the stored message, leaves the tab attached to the next submission, or stops opening when the prompt fires. All four were injected on this branch and measured, not reasoned about. Mutation 1, apiUserType returns the new role unchanged: 5 of 29 tests fail. Mutation 2, composeFeedbackText drops the tab line: 7 of 29 fail. Mutation 3, the widget no longer clears the tab after a save: 1 of 29 fails. Mutation 4, the widget stops listening for the open event: 6 of 29 fail. Mutation 5, added after the pre-push cross-review found that closing the form unsent left the tab and the feature-request type behind, removes the floating-button reset: 1 of 31 fails. Added when the prompt was also placed on the LMR and TOD tool page: mutation 6, the page no longer mounts the feedback form: 2 of 5 page tests fail. Mutation 7, the page no longer shows the prompt: 4 of 5 fail. Mutation 8, the page mounts the widget with its floating button on: 2 of 5 fail.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Yes, observed on this branch on 2026-11-15, not assumed. With apiUserType changed to return the role unchanged, the command printed 5 failed of 29 tests, among them the component test sends a new role as other and the three per-role helper cases. With the event listener removed from the widget it printed 6 failed of 29. With the tab line dropped from composeFeedbackText it printed 7 failed of 29. With the tab no longer cleared after a save it printed 1 failed of 29. The same command printed 0 failed of 29 on the unmodified code. For the LMR and TOD page, observed on 2026-11-15: removing the form mount printed 2 failed of 5, removing the prompt printed 4 failed of 5, and turning the floating button on printed 2 failed of 5; the unmodified page printed 0 failed of 5.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: The body the widget POSTs to /api/feedback is read from the mocked fetch call and asserted field by field, so the tests judge what leaves the browser for the real route and not the helper's own return value. The route's own fallback, userType || 'other' at app/api/feedback/route.ts, is the authority for why 'other' is a safe value to send.

pre_impl.existing_data: components/feedback/FeedbackWidget.tsx was already mounted on /assessment, posting to /api/feedback, which saves to user_feedback and emails the operator. It already had a Feature Request type and a role list. COMPONENT_MAP.md and the prior-art sweep found it before any code was written, so no second endpoint, table or email template was built.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: I first assumed a feedback button had to be added from scratch and that it should reuse the canibuildit lead route. Reading that route showed it sends confirmation emails and has per-type templates and verdict recomputation, which is far heavier than a feedback prompt. I also assumed I could check production's constraint on user_type; the read-only catalog query was denied by the permission classifier, so the design sends only values the column already holds.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Two small new files and no new endpoint or storage. FeedbackPrompt.tsx is a visible entry point only. lib/feedback-prompt.ts holds the event name, the extra roles and the text builder. Everything else is an edit to the existing widget and one mount line on the assessment page.

functions.name: apiUserType
functions.input: the role string chosen in the widget's I am a select, which may now be one of four new roles
functions.output: the string sent as user_type: the value itself only when it is one of the seven the widget has always sent, otherwise 'other'
functions.if_none: a new role, an unknown string or an empty value is sent as other, which the route also uses as its own fallback, so nothing outside the known set can reach the column

functions.name: composeFeedbackText
functions.input: the typed message plus the tab the form was opened from and the chosen role
functions.output: the message with a one-line bracketed prefix only when a tab or a new role exists, otherwise the message unchanged
functions.if_none: with no tab and an existing role the original text is returned untouched, which a test asserts, so the floating button's submissions are not altered

functions.name: FeedbackPrompt.handleClick
functions.input: a click on the Tell us what you were looking for button, with the current tab id as a prop
functions.output: one feedback_prompt_clicked event carrying only the tab, then a window event that opens the widget
functions.if_none: if PostHog throws, the error is swallowed and the form still opens, which a test asserts

break_it.scenario: Production's user_type column carries a CHECK constraint that rejects a value the new select offers, so every submission from that role fails with a 500.
break_it.what_happens: The visitor sees Failed to submit feedback and nothing is saved, the exact silent loss this change must not create. The constraint could not be read, because the read-only catalog query was denied.
break_it.how: The four new roles are never sent as user_type. apiUserType maps them to other, which the route already uses as its own fallback, and a test asserts the posted body. Mutation 1 shows the test fails if the role is sent unchanged.
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest --runTestsByPath __tests__/components/feedback/FeedbackPrompt.test.tsx -t "sends a new role as other"

break_it.scenario: The tab from one prompt-opened submission is still attached to the next submission made with the floating button.
break_it.what_happens: A later message about something else carries a From line naming a tab the visitor was no longer thinking about, which pollutes the stored feedback with a wrong location.
break_it.how: The widget clears the stored tab when a save succeeds. A test saves once from the prompt, waits for the reset, submits again from the floating button and asserts the second text has no prefix. Mutation 3 fails that test.
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest --runTestsByPath __tests__/components/feedback/FeedbackPrompt.test.tsx -t "does not carry the tab"

break_it.scenario: The prompt is shown on a page but the FeedbackWidget mount is removed from the same page in a later edit.
break_it.what_happens: Clicking the prompt counts a click and then nothing opens, so the page invites feedback it cannot take and nobody notices from the code.
break_it.how: Mitigated for the LMR and TOD tool page: its page test renders the real page, loads a result, clicks the prompt and asserts the form opens and the message saves, and mutation 6 (mount removed) fails 2 of 5 of those tests. NOT mitigated for /assessment, which still has no page-level test, so removing its mount there would pass every automated check; COMPONENT_MAP.md records the pairing, which is documentation and not enforcement.
break_it.repro: delete the FeedbackWidget element in frontend-nextjs/app/assessment/page.tsx, load /assessment with a property selected, click Tell us what you were looking for, and observe that no form opens; for the tool page run npx jest --runTestsByPath __tests__/app/tools/upzoning-check-feedback.test.tsx after deleting its FeedbackWidget line

break_it.scenario: A visitor opens the page before any property is loaded, or while it is loading.
break_it.what_happens: If the prompt appeared with no property it would invite feedback about a page that has shown nothing yet, and the stored message would carry a tab with no address.
break_it.how: The prompt is mounted inside the same block that renders the tabs, which only renders when loading is false and a property is selected. The widget's own floating button remains available at all other times.
break_it.repro: load /assessment with no address and confirm the blue strip is absent, then search an address and confirm it appears above the tab bar

break_it.scenario: A visitor opens the form from the prompt on one tab, closes it with the X without sending, and later uses the floating button to send an unrelated general message.
break_it.what_happens: The stored text starts with a From line naming the earlier tab and the type stays at feature request, so a general message is silently filed as a feature request from the wrong place. My first break-it entry on stale tabs claimed this was mitigated, but it only covered the path after a successful save.
break_it.how: Found by the pre-push cross-review (gpt-5.6-sol, confidence 0.98) and verified against the code before acting: the floating button only called setIsOpen(true). The button now clears the tab and resets the type to general when the form was last opened from the prompt, and leaves everything alone otherwise, which a second test asserts. The new test was written first and failed, then passed after the fix, and mutation 5 fails it again.
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest --runTestsByPath __tests__/components/feedback/FeedbackPrompt.test.tsx -t "closed unsent and reopened from the floating button"

mutation_analysis: Four mutations on the new and edited code, each run and each caught. Mutation 1 sends the new role unchanged: 5 of 29 fail, covering the helper cases and the component test that checks the posted userType. Mutation 2 drops the tab line: 7 of 29 fail, the widest, because every prompt-opened submission asserts its prefix. Mutation 3 stops clearing the tab after a save: 1 of 29 fails, the single test written for that case, so it is a real guard and not redundant. Mutation 4 removes the event listener: 6 of 29 fail, covering every test that opens the form from the prompt. Each run restored the original files, confirmed by hash. A first attempt crashed on a Windows text-decoding error after applying mutation 1 and left that file broken; it was restored from its backup immediately and the script was fixed to always restore in a finally block. After the push the advisory cross-review raised one MEDIUM finding, that the tab and the feature-request type survive closing the form unsent. It was real, my earlier report entry overstated the mitigation, and it was fixed test-first as mutation 5 records. A second advisory finding on the following push said apiUserType passed unknown role strings through unchanged. Verdict: not reachable from the page, because the select offers a fixed list, but the helper's own comment promised never to send a new value and the code did not enforce it, and a test asserted the pass-through. It is now a whitelist of the seven existing values with everything else sent as other; the test was changed first and failed, then passed, 70 of 70. The first version placed the prompt only on /assessment, the DCP, LEP and SEPP tabbed app. The owner pointed out that the LMR and TOD answer is shown on /tools/upzoning-check, which COMPONENT_MAP.md already described and which I had left alone. The prompt was added there in the same PR, with a launcher option so the public page gets no new floating button, and a render test of the real page. The ads landing page /duplex-check was deliberately not changed, because its design is a single-purpose conversion layout.
residual_risk: Production's constraint on user_type was never read, so the claim that other is safe rests on the route using it as its own fallback, not on the schema. The assessment page has no page-level test, so the prompt-and-widget pairing is checked by two components rendered together in a test, not by the real page. The prompt shows one message to every visitor regardless of role, and nothing yet measures whether it increases feedback; the feedback_prompt_clicked event exists to measure that. Traffic to this page was 355 visitors in 30 days in August 2026, so counts will be small and should be read as qualitative signals. /assessment still has no page-level test; the LMR and TOD tool page does.
